Marissa —

Draft language and priorities below; attaching a first-pass mapping spreadsheet (redwood_nist_mapping_v1.xlsx). High-level position for Horizon:

- Positioning: Redwood's hosted API is marketed as a general-purpose inference service. We do not represent the hosted endpoint as a purpose-built "high-risk" system under Annex III. However, because customers may deploy our outputs into high-impact decisions, we provide controls and evidence that enable customers to meet Annex III obligations.

- What we provide (Hosted / Dedicated / Private):
  • Evidence: model provenance, model version hashes, deployment timestamps (available for Dedicated/Private; selective artifacts available for Hosted under enterprise agreement)
  • Eval/Regression: continuous sampling and scheduled regression runs; metrics and alerting (details below)
  • Operations: audit logs (request/response headers, token usage), access controls, role-based admin; standard retention 12 months for Hosted, configurable for Dedicated/Private

- Quick canary/regression posture we can commit to for Horizon (Hosted):
  • Canary sampling: we can run a canary on a shadowed 1–2% of production traffic for 48–72 hours (no automatic routing changes; monitoring only)
  • Regression sampling: weekly batched regression on a representative prompt set (customer-supplied + Redwood-supplied), baseline comparison on guardrail metrics
  • Metrics: grounding/precision, hallucination/safety-policy hits, latency percentiles, top-k response divergence
  • Rollback triggers (suggested): >3 percentage point increase in safety-policy hits, or >5 percentage point drop in grounding precision relative to baseline; automatic rollback not available on Hosted (we will coordinate and initiate rollback), available for Dedicated/Private

I'll let Rishi add operational constraints and proposed SLAs.

Thanks Ben — good start. A few edits before we send:

- Tighten the Annex III language: state clearly that Redwood does not certify the hosted API as a "high-risk system" and that final product classification is the customer's responsibility; then list controls Redwood provides to enable Annex III compliance.
- Add concrete thresholds we can commit to in writing for the RFP packet (these are the numbers we'll share):
  • Canary: 2% shadow sampling for 72 hours (monitoring + alerting)
  • Regression sampling: weekly run using a combined 5,000 prompt sample set (customer + Redwood) or representative sampling equal to 1% of weekly traffic, whichever is larger
  • Failure thresholds for automated alerts: >3% relative increase in safety policy hits, or >5% relative decrease in grounding precision (measured as fraction of responses with verifiable source/grounding), or >7% increase in hallucination flag rate
  • Escalation: automated Slack/email paging to Horizon's named contacts + Redwood CSG on triggers
- Model operations and traceability: include that we store model build artifacts, git-like model hashes, and a changelog for each production variant; for Hosted customers this metadata is viewable in the Console for the last 12 months; Dedicated/Private offers extended provenance and archive access.
- Audit logs: default retention 12 months on Hosted; Enterprise packs can extend to 3 years.

Can Rishi confirm we can offer a signed attestation about regression cadence and the option for a third-party review if they require it? If so I'll finalize the draft and send to Alicia + Jordan with attachments (mapping + evidence index).
